title: Bearer-token extraction into an authentication dependency

steps.title: Choose the boundary: Bearer-token extraction into an authentication dependency

blocks.text: HTTPBearer extracts a presented credential from Authorization: Bearer token. Obtaining that credential does not establish validity.
On a handler input, declare Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())]. Read scheme and credentials for the supplied scheme and token text.
With default auto_error=True, missing credentials and non-bearer schemes are rejected before the handler. Test absent and malformed Authorization headers separately.

from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer

@app.get("/credential")
def handler(credential: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())]):
    scheme = credential.scheme
    token = credential.credentials
    return {"extracted": True}

client.get("/credential", headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer synthetic-token'})

client.get("/credential", headers={})

client.get("/credential", headers={'Authorization': 'Basic synthetic'})

client.get("/credential", headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer'})

steps.title: Trace the distinction: Bearer-token extraction into an authentication dependency

blocks.text: Trace four inputs separately: nonempty Bearer, absent header, non-bearer scheme, and Bearer without text. Only extraction is being examined. Even when scheme and credentials are available, that text is not proof of valid claims; do not return or log the supplied credential.

steps.title: Distinguish: Bearer-token extraction into an authentication dependency

correct.message: Default extraction rejects absent, Basic, and empty Bearer headers. A nonempty Bearer credential can reach the handler, but receiving it does not establish validity.

incorrect.message: Default extraction rejects absent, Basic, and empty Bearer headers. A nonempty Bearer credential can reach the handler, but receiving it does not establish validity.

public.prompt: Which statement correctly describes HTTPBearer’s default extraction behavior?

options.text: A nonempty Bearer credential reaches the handler, but extraction does not establish validity; absent, Basic, and empty Bearer headers are rejected.
Every Authorization header reaches the handler and is valid
A nonempty Bearer credential reaches the handler and extraction proves validity
Empty Bearer headers pass, but Basic headers are rejected.

o2.message: Not every header passes: absent, Basic, and empty Bearer credentials are rejected. Extracting a credential does not establish its validity.

o3.message: A nonempty Bearer credential can reach the handler, but extraction does not prove that credential is valid.

o4.message: Basic headers are rejected, but empty Bearer headers are also rejected; a nonempty Bearer credential is needed to pass extraction.

# BEGIN LEARNER EDITS
@app.get("/credential")
def credential(credential: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())]):
    # TODO: Declare the bearer dependency; assert the supplied scheme and credential inside the handler without returning or logging the credential; return {'accepted': True}.
    assert credential.scheme == 'Bearer'
    assert credential.credentials != ''
    return {'accepted': True}
# END LEARNER EDITS
